obligations.summary: Providers of general-purpose AI models meeting the condition in Article 51(1)(a) must notify the Commission without delay and within two weeks of that requirement being met or becoming known to be met, including information demonstrating the requirement has been met.
If the Commission becomes aware of a general-purpose AI model presenting systemic risks that has not been notified, it may designate it as a model with systemic risk.

Providers notifying the Commission under Article 52(1) may submit sufficiently substantiated arguments demonstrating that, despite meeting the threshold condition, their general-purpose AI model does not present systemic risks due to its specific characteristics.
exceptions: Provider may argue that specific characteristics of the model mean it does not present systemic risks despite meeting the Article 51(1)(a) threshold

obligations.summary: Where the Commission finds that the provider's arguments under Article 52(2) are insufficiently substantiated and systemic risks are not disproven, it must reject those arguments and classify the model as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk.

The Commission may designate a general-purpose AI model as presenting systemic risks ex officio or following a qualified alert from the scientific panel, based on criteria in Annex XIII, and is empowered to adopt delegated acts to amend Annex XIII.

Upon a reasoned request containing objective, detailed, and new reasons from a provider whose model was designated under Article 52(4), the Commission must take the request into account and may reassess the systemic risk designation, with providers eligible to request reassessment no earlier than six months after the designation decision.
exceptions: Reassessment may only be requested at the earliest six months after the designation decision or, after a maintained designation, six months after that subsequent decision

obligations.summary: The Commission must publish and keep up to date a list of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk, while observing protections for intellectual property rights, confidential business information, and trade secrets under Union and national law.
exceptions: Publication is subject to the need to protect intellectual property rights, confidential business information, and trade secrets in accordance with Union and national law
